spans.text: Inside Amaris' neural cloud.
The pale moon hangs high above the fated twins. The two of them face each other in this silent realm, as streams of data flow past them.
You won't be able to kill me with just this much.
Did you use all your strength just to keep me in the depths of your neural cloud for just a bit longer?
...Aliana.
How on earth did you kill them?
I can't even recover their neural cloud cores...
I've told you many times, dear sister.
It was through the final resting place of every soldier—their "dog tags".
That is also why I can find you, and only you, no matter where you are.
Now that I've answered your question, its time for you to answer mine.
You... Why were you in the "Daybreak" squad?
You'll find out soon enough.
Amaris smiles. This is an expression Aliana has never seen her make before.
Aliana, why do you think I am the "moon"?
In the endless darkness, Amaris takes a seat in a corner of this unviewable realm.
Drip...
It is as though a drop of water has fallen into this still, stagnant, dead water.
In the next moment, cool moonlight chases away the darkness and scatters the fog before Amaris' eyes.
You...
The light is so gentle that even Amaris, who has been in the dark all this time, does not feel any discomfort viewing it.
Congratulations on finding your whole self.
Congratulations.
Well done, Amaris.
...I always knew you could do it
Well, I've got to hand it to you now.
How does it feel to be "Amaris" again?
You guys...
(Applause)
The darkness is fully gone now, and one familiar face after another appears before Amaris.
She stares dumbly at them from her seat, unwilling even to blink, as though they might leave if she did.
Drip...
A tear courses down her cheek, but she doesn't notice at all.
Amaris.
A hand gently pats her shoulder. Amaris shudders, then slowly looks up to see Eula standing beside her, smiling as kindly as always.
Eula...
Amaris' tears obscure her vision.
In the data realm of the base layer, physical obstructions are meaningless.
She knows full well that this is just an outcome she is trying to avoid.
Amaris!
It is Eula's voice that reawakens her.
Are you... going to leave me now?
Eula looks at her and gently pats her head.
Amaris, I've always known that you had the strength and bravery that we didn't.
You knew the truth and what you had to do from the beginning, didn't you?
Heh, don't worry about us. I don't want to be a bad big sister who drags her little sister down at the end.
Aliana was once the sun that illuminated us.
But to us, you are the patient moon.
Amaris... this is a duty that only you can perform.
Are you ready, Amaris?
Don't be scared. We're all by your side.
Amaris nods.
All the familiar faces close in around her like a loop. Some are kind, some encouraging, and some are approving.
As she bathes in their gazes, Amaris sighs heavily before slowly lifting her head.
...Tell us. Who are you?
I am the moon that swallows the sun.
Just like how the eclipse is the shadow that swallows all daylight.
She is the last sister of "Daybreak", the one who was loved by all—these memories and this support have allowed her to be selfish and survive until now.
This selfishness nearly made her forget her duty, which was to serve as the "fatal flaw" for a certain someone.
...I am Amaris.
Your name has been chosen.
Daughter of the Moon, a gift from the gods.
Amaris.
Thus, we have decided to give you a little gift of our own.
...What is it?
It is a door, one that you will use to store a little redundant data in your neural cloud space for the future of Daybreak Squad.
Are you willing to strive hard for the future of Daybreak Squad?
...I am.
Good. Her end will also be your beginning.
The key to this door is yours now, but you must not use it lightly.
Lock these memories away for now, for when the time comes... No, that time should never come.
The seat below Amaris has already vanished.
She is standing now, her head held up high as her tightly-shut eyelids begin to open. There is no longer any doubt in her shining eyes.
Eula, Laurel, Callisto... One familiar face after another stands behind her.
The Dog Tag System, you say?
The thing that destroyed and imprisoned you.
...Today, I will put an end to all this.
The door bound by steel chains that glows with a dangerous light sits quietly before her.
Amaris reaches out to it without a second thought.
Eula's hand covers hers.
Laurel's hand covers hers.
Callisto's hand covers hers.
One after another, their ephemeral shades overlap with her hand.
Amaris does not look back, even though she knows there is nobody behind her.
Creak—
The heavy chains snap one by one, putting up no resistance whatsoever. The door that always rejected Amaris finally begins to open for her.
Whoosh—
A stream of data she's never seen before suddenly floods into this domain.
The phantasmal moon overhead grows brighter. Beneath its light, people and objects that did not originally exist in this place appear before her eyes once again.
...I see, so it was you.
I'm so happy it was you, Amaris!
You have three minutes to say your last words.
Pfft, you're so cute when you act tough, Aliana.
Samantha's smile slowly vanishes, and she lowers her eyes.
The death of humans on a battlefield is always a very painful thing.
The melding of neural clouds is just a forced merging of data, so it shouldn't hurt so much, right...
Frankly speaking, I don't know.
Tell me, Aliana, will there be an end to war?
This is what I should be doing.
Although I already knew this, I still couldn't convince myself when the time came.
Whether I was blown up by a stray bomb, or melted down by the enemy...
There is a long silence.
Samantha closes her eyes and her body shudders.
Aliana reaches out her hand and places it on Samantha's chest.
A blue light glows.
Ali, no matter who lives in the end, please remember our mission, to end the war and bring back the light of day...
That way, it'll be as though we completed our mission...
Samantha's face grows paler and paler.
Her neural cloud data is forcefully extracted and fused...
A massive stream of data quickly takes shape.
Samantha's sorrow, fear, pain and resignation... they all flow into it.
These rich feelings tear at Aliana's neural cloud and make her feel like she's split into two Dolls.
(Pants heavily)
Hah—Dammit.
I always wanted a proper showdown.
Still, there's no chance for that; you took me out so quickly...
I didn't think the end would be so boring...
...Is that all you have to say?
What else is there to say?
Wars end when the bullets run out.
I just didn't expect you to fire the last shot...
There will be an end to war.
Unfortunately, it's got nothing to do with me.
It's got nothing to do with the tens of thousands of people who have died all these years too.
Do it, don't make me suffer.
Daybreak will come eventually, for one person or another...
Callisto's image wavers and is eventually consumed and shredded by the flood. Aliana's face grows paler.
It's sad... But although it's sad, I feel nothing.
Am I broken?
Why... I don't understand... Why...
Aliana...
Aliana...
Bang—!
Aliana pulls the trigger and blasts the final phantom, Eula, to bits.
Eula's cold face becomes Amaris' face. This time, one of them is still looking haughtily down on the others, but their positions are reversed now.
Like a poison deep in her bones, all that data runs rampant throughout Aliana's body.
Her body is torn apart and put back together over and over again, barely managing to hold onto its original shape.
She looks at Amaris before her and smiles thinly.
You win.
After I die, will you inherit my memory fragments like you did theirs?
I won't. You don't deserve to be in the same room as them, even as fragments.
...That's a relief. I hate the feeling of being watched. Even if it's by you, Amaris.
Heh. I can't kill you like you killed them.
What a shame... You won't be able to take my dog tags...
I've already taken back everyone's things.
Have you?
And you... Aliana... You don't matter any more.
At least, not to me.
Your "Dog Tag" system is bound to my "Door".
...I see...
Or rather, they're the same system when they're put together.
However, they felt that you were the future of Daybreak Squad.
That's why they gave you everything that could improve your capabilities.
Haha, lucky me, then—
And... All the things they considered useless, like accumulated emotions and redundant memory data, they gave to me instead.
Thanks to that design, they've been keeping me company for 13 years.
Amaris' voice trails off, as though she's lost interest.
Clatter.
The howling night wind bursts into the center of the skyscraper through the broken windows, and it sounds like wailing as it blows through the building's interior.
Aliana is lying in the center of the structure, staring dazedly at Amaris, who is standing tall before her.
Amaris looks at Aliana, who has collapsed and is powerless to stand back up. She takes a piece of paper from her waistpouch and tosses it at Aliana.
The paper spins in the wind as it falls, and it finally lands beside Aliana's head.
It is a picture of two people.
Amaris looks Aliana dead in the eyes.
Aliana returns her gaze, staring deep into her eyes.
It is only then that Aliana realizes something.
The weak, useless Amaris that always needed to be cared for by others...
At some point, when she was not aware of it, she had sprouted, blossomed, and grown into a towering tree that even she could not budge.
Did you know? I used to envy you.
And for a moment, just a moment, I wondered if I should become you.
And yes, I did dream of becoming someone like you.
Aliana doesn't say a word. She can speak, but right now, she chooses not to.
But right now, that place...
The place that I always admired and longed to reach...
The person standing there isn't you anymore.
As she looks at Aliana's dull eyes, Amaris wipes her face and turns away.
This is a determination she has never shown before.
Aliana looks at the empty ceiling.
She listens to the endless, hollow echoes of footsteps.
Finally, they vanish in the direction of the exit.
...The night is silent once more.
